title: Pluglet SDK compact bootkit — quickstart & sprint notes
content:
Context and intent:

This is a working note for a compact, opinionated SDK 'bootkit' we call Pluglet. Goal: get an engineering teammate (or small product team) from 0 to a production-like integration in < 2 hours with minimal infra or config. Focus on: one-page quickstart, tiny reproducible samples across JS/Python/Rust, local cassette mocking, telemetry-first safety hooks, and an onboarding checklist for SEs.

Why a compact bootkit?
- Many existing SDK docs dive deep; new adopters want a tiny path that demonstrates value fast (embedding generation, chat streaming, cost-metering).
- We want to standardize the minimal surface area that internal integrators and early external adopters need: auth, sample request, simple retry/fallback, and visibility into per-request cost/latency.

Core principles (decision log):
1) One obvious path: minimal friction, opinionated defaults.
2) Polyglot parity: same examples in JS, Python, and a short Rust snippet (not a full crate).
3) Telemetry-first: every quickstart shows token/cost/latency output by default.
4) Local-first dev loop: cassette/mock runtime so you can iterate offline.
5) Enable graceful degradation: local stub -> hosted API -> dedicated fallback.

Quickstart (one-page) outline (target < 10 steps):
1) Install pluglet: npm/pip/cargo example.
   - npm: npm i @redwood/pluglet
   - pip: pip install redwood-pluglet
   - rust: cargo add pluglet-slim (note: minimal shim example)
2) Create minimal config file (~6 lines): api_key, project, telemetry: on, cassette: enabled.
3) Run a sample generation: pluglet quick-run --model gpt-redwood-1 --prompt "Summarize..."
4) View local cassette (./fixtures/cassettes/latest.json) to inspect request/response and token breakdown.
5) Wire streaming into UI: short sample showing EventSource/WebSocket fallback for partial tokens.
6) Flip to live mode: pluglet migrate --mode hosted (explain env var change).
7) Run telemetry checker: pluglet check-telemetry (validates traces are emitted and cost tags exist).
8) Optional: run smoke test to validate retry/fallback rules.
9) Deploy snippet for serverless function with example CI step.

Minimal example content we should include on the page (snippets):
- JS (5 lines) to get a chat response and show token/cost summary
- Python (5 lines) same behavior
- Rust (2–3 lines) show how to call the shim and unwrap text

Local cassette mode (developer loop):
- cassette mode captures first real request and then replays it for offline iteration.
- files are stored under ./pluglet/cassettes/{project}/{scenario}.json
- cassette includes request metadata: model, seq_len_stats, kv_cache_hint, tokens_in/tokens_out, cost_estimate.
- Commands: pluglet cassette record --name demo ; pluglet cassette replay --name demo --port 8081

Telemetry & observability defaults:
- Each request emits: request_id, model_version, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, cost_usd_est.
- Telemetry sinks: console (dev), opentelemetry/OTLP (prod), and a lightweight local file for quick inspection.
- Sanity check command checks for per-route instrumentation and sample prompts.

Safety and failure modes to surface in quickstart:
- Show how to configure a simple content filter hook: if response contains matched patterns -> route to fallback model (smaller/safer).
- Demonstrate a retry policy that does not double-bill (idempotency + idempotency key header).
- Show timeout/abort example to prevent long-running tokens in UI flows.

Developer experience checklist (for SEs running a lightweight demo):
- [ ] Confirm API key creation flow documented (1-click copy).
- [ ] Confirm example outputs include token/cost lines by default.
- [ ] Ensure cassette can be toggled on/off without code change (env var override).
- [ ] Confirm streaming example works behind a corporate proxy (note common failure: chunked transfer blocked).
- [ ] Provide one-click Cloud Run/Heroku sample deploys with minimal env vars.

Sprint plan (T-shirt sized tasks):
- Spike (1 day): assemble the 1-page quickstart and sample repos for JS+Python+Rust.
- Telemetry hookup (2 days): build simple pluglet check-telemetry and local file sink.
- Cassette mechanics (3 days): record/replay, format decisions, include token breakdown.
- UX polish (2 days): one-click runnable demo links + GitHub Codespaces config.
- Docs + QA (2 days): internal review, smoke-run across mac/linux, and proxy testing.

Open questions / unresolved decisions (notes to self):
- How opinionated should default models be? Do we pin to a curated tiny model for demos or default to 'latest-hosted'?
- Token/cost math: include rough estimate per model in quickstart or link to a dynamic calculator?
- Rust ergonomics: do we maintain a tiny wrapper crate or just show FFI curl examples?
- Cassette privacy: recorded cassettes may capture PII — add an optional scrubber step on first record.

Guides to author on first pass (short list for content owners):
- 1-page quickstart (hero): minimal flow + 3 code snippets + one GIF of 'first response'
- Local dev guide: cassette usage, debugging token counts, replaying network failures
- SE runbook: checklist + common Slack/GitHub troubleshooting links
- Reference: telemetry schema + sample OTLP collector config

Notes for implementation team (engineering constraints):
- Keep npm package < 200KB minified for fast installs; split devDeps.
- Vanilla JS runtime support: support Deno and Node; avoid heavy bundlers in examples.
- Python: support 3.10+; avoid optional native deps to keep pip install simple.
- Rust: make example optional via feature flag in repo; avoid heavy async runtime dependencies for the tiny shim.

Next immediate actions (who / when):
- Maya: draft one-page quickstart and regenerate with real sample responses (due 2025-09-19)
- Liam: spike cassette JSON schema + minimal recorder integration (due 2025-09-22)
- Priya: design one GIF and confirm copy for 'first 2 minutes' landing (due 2025-09-24)
- Ethan: add CI job that runs quickstart smoke test in GitHub Actions (due 2025-09-26)

Feedback loop and review:
- Post draft to #devexp-quickstarts channel; collect 3 internal reviews before public draft.
- Link to test-run checklist in PR template (see linked artifacts).
